source_checks.finding: Page is for Gmail on a computer. Steps 1 to 7 match the page: open Gmail on your computer; Settings icon then See all settings; General tab, Vacation responder section; Vacation responder on; date range, subject and message; optional checkbox to send the reply to contacts only, under the message; Save Changes. The page excerpt 'In most cases, your reply is only sent to people the first time they message you.' is verbatim on the page but is not used in the target.

Verbatim on the page: 'Your automatic reply starts at 12:00 AM on the start date and ends at 11:59 PM on the end date, unless you end it earlier.' The page places this under the heading 'Learn how an automatic reply works', not 'Conditions'. The claim itself is correct; the section label in the ref should be corrected.

required_actions.action: Turn on the vacation responder in Gmail on the computer
Set the start date to December 1 and the end date to December 8 (user's stated dates)
Limit the reply to contacts only, using the checkbox under the message (user asked for this)
Note that the reply runs from 12:00 AM on the start date to 11:59 PM on the end date unless ended early
Click Save Changes at the bottom of the page

findings: The user gave the dates December 1 to December 8, but step 5 says only 'Enter a date range, a subject, and a message.' The target does not apply the user's dates.

The user asked for replies only to contacts, but step 6 begins 'Optional:' and the target never answers the user's question 'Is it possible' with a yes. The user's stated choice is not respected as a plain instruction.
The reviewer checks the page for the dates and contacts-only option; both are on the page, so the fix only needs to tailor the wording.
correction_required: Add one line before step 1: 'Yes, you can limit the reply to your contacts.' Replace step 5 with: 'Enter December 1 as the start date and December 8 as the end date, then enter a subject and a message.' Replace step 6 with: 'To send replies only to your contacts, check the box below the message.' Keep steps 1 to 4 and 7, and keep the closing line about 12:00 AM and 11:59 PM unchanged.

source_checks.finding: Page is for Gmail on a computer. In the Tips part of the setup section, the page says: 'When your vacation responder is on, a banner shows across the top of your inbox.' and 'To turn it off, click End now.' Both claims are on the page and match the target.

required_actions.action: Find the banner across the top of the inbox, which shows while the responder is on
Click End now to turn the responder off

source_checks.finding: Page covers Gmail on a computer. The create-label steps (On the left, next to 'Labels', click Create new label; enter a label name; optional 'Nest label under'; click Create) are on the page. The excerpt 'Labels are different from folders.' is verbatim, but it sits in the page's key-distinction text, not in the Create a label section. The page does not use the word 'icon'; the passage's 'icon' wording is a description of the control, not a label, and is accepted.

required_actions.action: Open Gmail on the computer
Click Create new label next to Labels in the left sidebar
Enter a name for the label (for example, the school)
Click Create
Nesting under another label; the user did not ask for it, so it is a distractor kept as optional
Apply the label to existing school emails (page section Apply a label to an existing email, not in the passage; not required by the passage, so not a finding)

source_checks.finding: Page covers Gmail on a computer. The page steps match: check the box next to the email; at the top, click Labels; uncheck the current label; select the new label. The page says 'To move an email instead: Uncheck the current label.' The excerpt 'Labels are different from folders.' is verbatim but sits in the key-distinction text, not in the section cited. The page says 'Labels' rather than 'Labels icon'; the word icon is accepted as a description of the control.

required_actions.action: Check the box next to the email
Click Labels at the top
Uncheck the wrong label
Select the right label

source_checks.finding: Page covers Google Account on a computer. Steps match: go to myaccount.google.com; Security & sign-in; under 'How you sign in to Google', Recovery phone; follow the steps on the screen. The page says 'You might need to sign in.' The passage and target say 'You may need to sign in first'; the added word 'first' is not on the page, which is a card wording fix, not a reason to revise. The sentence 'Recovery info helps you get back into your account and helps keep your account secure.' is verbatim, under 'How recovery info is used', not the cited section. The page also lists 'Someone else uses your account' as a reason recovery info helps, which supports the user's concern.

required_actions.action: Open myaccount.google.com
Select Security & sign-in
Select Recovery phone under How you sign in to Google, signing in if asked
Complete the on-screen prompts
User has no recovery phone or email, so no edit or delete step is needed (completed state, not repeated)

source_checks.finding: Page covers Google Account on a computer. Steps match: go to myaccount.google.com; Security & sign-in; under 'How you sign in to Google', Recovery email; next to your email, click Edit to change it or Delete to remove it; follow the steps on the screen. The page says 'You might need to sign in' rather than 'You may need to sign in first'; the added word 'first' is not on the page, a card wording fix only. The recovery info sentence is verbatim, but it sits under 'How recovery info is used', not the cited Add or change a recovery email address section.

required_actions.action: Open myaccount.google.com
Select Security & sign-in
Select Recovery email under How you sign in to Google, signing in if asked
Next to the old email, click Edit to change it
Complete the on-screen prompts
Delete option is a distractor; the user wants to change the address, not remove it (kept in the target as the other choice on the same line)
